newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK - BANK STOCKS LIFT INDEX.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK - BANK STOCKS LIFT INDEX.

text.p: For the third week in
succession, bank stocks took the market higher, but some sellers
appeared and began to take profits.
The index rose 45.98 points to close at 723.45 with domestic
market capitalisation up seven percent. The foreign index shed
50.53 points to close at 378.51. The all companies index dropped
58.20 points to 386.90.
The three bank stocks now account for over 50 percent of the
domestic capitalisation.
Barclays Bank of Botswana jumped 300 thebe to
1,700 thebe on the back of 67,140 shares traded, First National
Bank put on 190 thebe to 775 thebe with 14,500 shares
traded and Standard Chartered Bank of Botswana added 100
thebe to 1,450 thebe and traded 7,800 shares.
Of the remaining nine counters, seven traded.
Botswana Insurance crossed 200,000 shares at an
undisclosed special price, but closed unchanged at 305 thebe,
security group Inco traded in small volume closing
unchanged at 105 thebe, variable loan stock company RDC
Properties also traded small volume and was unchanged
at 180 thebe, as did food and tobacco wholesaler Metsef
closing 5 thebe up at 685 thebe.
There were reasonable volumes traded in clothing chain Pep
and milling company and food wholesaler Sefalana, Pep Holdings
put on 5 thebe to close at 380 thebe and Sefalana
Holdings closed 20 thebe up at 550 thebe.
Brewery holding company Sechaba Trust moved the
largest volume of the week, 600,300 shares, but traded unchanged
at 480 thebe.
Untraded and unchanged were investment company Kgolo ya
Sechaba , bid 30 thebe closing 30 thebe and oil company
Engen bid 480t, closed 450t.
Total domestic volume was down with 933,440 (1,399,450)
shares traded for value 4,966,520 (6,993,070) pula.
Of the six foreign dual listed counters, car rental and
fleet management group Avis and furniture group Profurn were the
only ones to trade. Avis moved 800 shares to close 26
thebe up at 758 thebe, Profun traded 40,600 shares and
closed 14 thebe up at 226 thebe.
Untraded were De Beers dropping 1,919 thebe after
the less than sparkling interim result to close at 12,004 thebe
and largely accounting for the 22 percent drop in market cap on
the foreign board, professional services group Forbes
down 38 thebe to 746 thebe, McCarthy Retail group was
up 13 thebe to 1,210 and Regent Undervalued Assets Fund
unchanged at 4,000 thebe.
